title: Dogs’ Brains Can Read Some Human Emotions
summary:
Dogs may tell some human feelings apart by looking at faces. Scientists trained 14 family dogs to lie still in an MRI scanner that watches brain activity.

Laura Cuaya’s team at the University of Vienna showed the dogs photos of faces. Happy faces lit up a reward area in the brain more than neutral faces. Angry or sad faces caused different brain patterns than fearful faces.

The results were shared in the journal iScience. Cuaya says this is the first evidence dogs can tell different negative emotions apart on faces.

The study used border collies and golden retrievers, so other breeds might differ. Still, it is another reason to smile at a dog you meet.
why_it_matters: Understanding dog feelings helps kids treat pets with more care and respect.
